Plantations palm oil, tea

Researched in Agriculture & plantations

Adopt first

Have estate maps and a drone pilot or contracted drone service; start with one block and compare imagery readings with agronomist checks; expect ongoing flight, data-processing and agronomy staffing.

Precision agronomy: drones with multispectral imaging, soil and weather sensors (moisture, temperature, light, pH), satellite data; ML recommends fertilisation and irrigation

Where
MY, Southeast Asia
Segment
SMB and enterprise estates
Problem
land-management inefficiency reduces yield; climate uncertainty
Technology
drones, multispectral imaging, soil/weather sensors, satellite data, ML recommendations, automated irrigation
Who uses it
plantation managers and operators on palm oil and tea estates; 'several large plantation companies' (unnamed)
Outcome
AI image processing 10,000 ha in 4 h vs 14+ days for 20 people (company's own figure, reported by Bloomberg); no yield figures
Effort
high
Risks
Recommendation accuracy unproven without yield data; dependence on drone or analytics vendors; skills gaps on estates.

How to adopt

Have estate maps and a drone pilot or contracted drone service; start with one block and compare imagery readings with agronomist checks; expect ongoing flight, data-processing and agronomy staffing.

How a room runs it

the ROOM for an estate block: the estate manager, the field supervisor and an agronomy teammate (an agent definition with the plantation skills); the agent reads the readings and imagery the estate already has and GENERATES the week's tasks for the supervisor (which plots to irrigate, dose, inspect) as plan steps with owners and due dates, and the manager's advisory as a decision block with a deadline; what the humans keep: the field work, the sign-off, the spend above the envelope; the receipt records every finished task

The engagement on top

a custom engagement: the estate's own systems stay theirs — the agent is wired to them through connectors loaded on this pull (sensor feeds, the imagery folder, the ERP), the agronomist joins as the paid professional on the match, and the sector pack carries the vocabulary and the task templates

Source: press · 2019

Early detection of abnormal conditions (pests, disease) from imagery and sensors so managers act before damage spreads

Where
MY, Southeast Asia
Segment
enterprise estates
Problem
pests and disease
Technology
drones, satellite anomaly detection, ML pattern detection
Who uses it
estate managers
Outcome
none stated
Effort
medium
Risks
No detection rate given, so false alarms and misses are unknown; drone flight regulation; connectivity at remote estates.

How to adopt

Subscribe to satellite hot-spot alerts for estate boundaries; use drones to verify hard-to-reach sites; assign a manager to act on each alert.

How a room runs it

the same room: an alert from imagery or sensors becomes a TASK for the field team (inspect block 7 by Thursday) generated by the teammate, and a DECISION for the manager (treat / wait) with the evidence attached; nobody reads a dashboard — the work arrives as tasks and a decision in the Inbox

The engagement on top

inspection and treatment tasks handed to field staff over WhatsApp (the channel is built); the agronomist's verdict as a receipt

Source: press · 2019

Targeted irrigation and dosing: automated irrigation that activates only when needed; lower water and fertiliser use

Where
ID, Southeast Asia
Segment
SMB and enterprise
Problem
resource waste
Technology
automated irrigation, edge computing on site, cloud for storage and long-term analysis
Who uses it
operators
Outcome
Up to 20 % cost savings and up to 15 % yield improvement, reported by unnamed plantation companies (vendor page; no measurer named); a Heriot-Watt paper (Sustainability 2023, Malaysia) reports positive return on investment above 1.5 ha but gives no figures
Effort
high
Risks
Vendor figures unsourced; sensor failure or drift wastes water; single-vendor lock-in.

How to adopt

Install soil-moisture sensors and controllable valves on a pilot block; set thresholds with an agronomist; budget for sensor maintenance and connectivity.

How a room runs it

the teammate schedules irrigation and dosing as tasks against the plots' baselines and raises a decision when a plot drifts over its input budget — the budget envelope is the plot's, the wall degrades before it blocks

Source: vendor · 2024 · one vendor source; to corroborate

Harvest-timing prediction feeding logistics planning, 'faster and more transparent' distribution; centralised cloud records for 'long-term analysis and compliance'

Where
ID, Southeast Asia
Segment
enterprise
Problem
logistics and traceability; compliance
Technology
ML harvest prediction, cloud records
Who uses it
estates, buyers, logistics
Outcome
Up to 20 % cost savings and up to 15 % yield improvement, reported by unnamed plantation companies (vendor page; no measurer named); no figure for harvest prediction
Effort
medium
Risks
Forecast quality depends on clean historical data; vendor-only evidence; cloud data hosting and compliance questions.

How to adopt

Digitise harvest and delivery records first; then add forecasting on that history; connect to logistics and buyer planning.

How a room runs it

each harvest lot is a deliverable the teammate opens, routes to logistics as tasks, and closes with a receipt a buyer can verify; the compliance file is the record, not a separate system

The engagement on top

export deal rooms later (D261 — another monorepo on the public doors)

Source: vendor · 2024 · one vendor source; to corroborate

Barriers: skilled labour limited, connectivity limits on plantations, climate uncertainty — technology 'to support rather than replace farmers'

Where
MY, Southeast Asia
Segment
all
Problem
adoption barriers
Technology
edge computing for offline analysis
Who uses it
all actors
Outcome
Mata Aerotech's drone services covered 200,000 ha of oil palm estates; about 1,000 commercial drones in Malaysia (industry sources, unattributed); no quantified labour saving
Effort
medium
Risks
Robotics immature; workforce resistance or displacement; connectivity limits on plantations.

How to adopt

Treat labour shortage as the business case: pick one labour-heavy task (spraying, monitoring), pilot drones or machines on it, train existing staff to operate them.

How a room runs it

the room meets the barriers as it is: field staff work over WhatsApp with an agent that tolerates offline entry; the advice arrives in Bahasa; the agent supports the supervisor and never replaces the sign-off

Source: press · 2019

Machine plucking expanded to offset a manual labour shortage, drones applying fertiliser and pesticide and supervising farm practice, and AI being explored for efficiency and quality in Ceylon tea

Where
LK, South Asia
Segment
enterprise (listed tea and coffee estates)
Problem
manual labour shortage and rising production costs
Technology
machine plucking, agricultural drones, AI (exploratory)
Who uses it
Hatton Plantations (Sri Lanka); chairman G.D. Seaton (annual report 2024/2025)
Outcome
none stated (no tea productivity or cost figures given; the article cites only an 18 % electricity cut and a 500 ha coffee estate)
Effort
high
Risks
Machine plucking can lower leaf quality; labour displacement; no productivity figures published; drone rules.

How to adopt

Pick the most labour-bound task (plucking or spraying), pilot machines or drones on one division, train existing staff to operate them, then extend.

How a room runs it

the ROOM for a tea estate division; the estate manager, the field officers, the drone operator and a plantation teammate (an agent definition with the tea skills); the agent reads the plucking and drone-flight logs the estate already keeps and GENERATES the week's plucking-round, spray and fertiliser jobs for the field officers (block, product, window) as plan steps with owners and due dates, and raises a decision for the manager when a block's input spend passes its envelope (approve more / hold) in the Inbox as a proposal with a deadline; the humans keep the plucking, the flying, the sign-off and the spend above the envelope; the receipt records each finished job with block, product and date; budgets degrade before they block

The engagement on top

a custom engagement: the estate's field-record sheet or ERP and the drone operator's flight log wired to the room through connectors loaded on this pull, an agronomist or plantation accountant as the paid professional on the match, and the sector pack's task templates for the recurring rounds; the client receives the reports and gives direction in the room

Source: press · 2025

Drone mapping of oil palm estates: an orthomosaic map, an ML tree count and GIS identification of empty planting spaces for replanting, delivered on a web platform

Where
CI, Africa
Segment
enterprise (private palm estates)
Problem
no accurate estate map or tree inventory for planning replanting
Technology
fixed-wing survey drone (Wingtra One), photogrammetry software, machine learning tree counting, GIS
Who uses it
United Oil Company (Ivory Coast, about 16,300 ha across three plantations); Ghana Flying Labs; SKT Live
Outcome
none stated (the article says the mapping ensured accurate data but gives no counts or accuracy)
Effort
medium
Risks
Vendor-only evidence; count accuracy unreported; reliance on an outside survey provider; data ownership.

How to adopt

Commission a drone survey of one plantation, check the tree count against a ground sample, and use the gap map to plan replanting.

How a room runs it

the ROOM for a palm estate's replanting programme; the estate manager, the replanting supervisor, the survey contractor and a palm teammate; the agent reads the tree-count and gap map the contractor delivers and GENERATES the replanting rounds for the supervisor (block, number of palms, planting window) with due dates as plan steps with owners and due dates, and raises a decision for the manager (approve the seedling order, with a deadline) in the Inbox as a proposal with a deadline; the humans keep the survey flight, the planting and the spend above the envelope; the receipt records each map delivered, each block replanted and each seedling order; budgets degrade before they block

The engagement on top

a custom engagement: the estate's block register and the survey contractor's map files wired to the room through connectors loaded on this pull, a survey contractor or agronomist as the paid professional on the match, and the sector pack's task templates for the recurring rounds; the client receives the reports and gives direction in the room

Source: vendor · 2024 · vendor only; to corroborate

Sensor-based smart irrigation and fertigation for oil palm: soil-moisture and weather sensors send data over IoT to a dashboard that advises irrigation and fertigation, on two hectares of a research farm with two local growers; the study also compared irrigation systems

Where
CO, Latin America
Segment
enterprise and growers (pilot with research body)
Problem
irrigation of oil palm in a dry region wastes water; growers have not adopted efficient irrigation
Technology
soil-moisture and weather sensors, IoT, an advisory dashboard, drip, sprinkler and fertigation systems, water harvesting
Who uses it
Delphy (Netherlands) with Solidaridad Network, FutureWater and Cenipalma (the research arm of Fedepalma, Colombia); the Dutch Embassy in Colombia; two growers
Outcome
Efficient irrigation in the Sevilla basin could save up to 67 % of water with sprinklers and up to 72 % with drip (project study; sprinkler theft is the main barrier)
Effort
high
Risks
Estimates are for one basin; sprinkler theft; upfront cost of drip; sensor upkeep.

How to adopt

Install sensors on a small demonstration block, compare irrigation options on cost and water use, and choose the system the site can protect from theft.

How a room runs it

the ROOM for a palm grower and the research farm; the grower, the farm's irrigation technician and an irrigation teammate; the agent reads the soil-moisture and weather feed the sensor dashboard already produces and GENERATES the irrigation and fertigation rounds for the technician (block, volume, window) with due dates as plan steps with owners and due dates, and raises a decision for the grower when water or input spend passes its envelope (approve more / hold) in the Inbox as a proposal with a deadline; the humans keep the valve and pump work, the sign-off and the spend above the envelope; the receipt records each irrigation round with block and volume; budgets degrade before they block

The engagement on top

a custom engagement: the sensor dashboard export and the water-use sheet wired to the room through connectors loaded on this pull, an irrigation engineer as the paid professional on the match, and the sector pack's task templates for the recurring rounds; the client receives the reports and gives direction in the room

Source: gov · 2021

Mechanised tea plucking: a growers' agency subsidiary designed battery-powered plucking machines for smallholders with credit purchase; a listed estate invested in mechanised plucking and cut 267 jobs in 2023

Where
KE, Africa
Segment
smallholders and listed estate
Problem
hand-plucking cost and labour supply
Technology
battery-powered plucking machines, credit financing
Who uses it
Tea Machinery Company (Temec, subsidiary of Kenya Tea Development Agency); Greenland Fedha; Sasini Plc (Kenya)
Outcome
Sasini cut 267 jobs in 2023 and staff costs from Kes381.9 million to Kes359.9 million (Sasini statements as reported)
Effort
medium
Risks
Leaf quality below buyer standard; worker resistance and job loss; cost of machines to small growers.

How to adopt

Start with a shared machine for a group of growers on a credit or hire plan, check leaf quality against the buyer standard, and plan for the labour effects.

How a room runs it

the ROOM for a smallholder tea group; the group's chair, the growers, the plucking-machine operator and a tea teammate; the agent reads the group's plot list and the factory delivery records and GENERATES the plucking rounds and machine-booking steps for the operator (plot, day) with due dates as plan steps with owners and due dates, and raises a decision for each grower (book the machine and its fee, with a deadline) in the Inbox as a proposal with a deadline; the humans keep the plucking, the leaf-quality call and the payment; the receipt records each plot plucked, the leaf delivered and the machine fee, split across growers; budgets degrade before they block

The engagement on top

a custom engagement: the group's member register and the factory's leaf-delivery statements wired to the room through connectors loaded on this pull, a cooperative accountant or agronomist as the paid professional on the match, and the sector pack's task templates for the recurring rounds; the client receives the reports and gives direction in the room

Source: press · 2025

Agriculture A01

Researched in Agriculture & plantations

Adopt first

Trial spraying drones on a small share of fields with a distributor; train operators; check licensing and spray rules.

Drone trial for spraying, fertiliser and seed spreading on rice paddies: 15 ha of about 5,000 ha trialled since early 2025; tasks that needed at least ten people done by one operator in a few hours (company quote)

Where
ID, Southeast Asia
Segment
public / state-owned enterprise
Problem
labour-heavy field operations on large paddy estates; chemical use
Technology
autonomous agricultural drones (XAG P100 Pro), local distributor support
Who uses it
Sang Hyang Seri (state-owned rice company, Indonesia); PT Blessed Bentara Agri Indonesia (distributor)
Outcome
Tasks needing 10+ people done by one operator in a few hours (company quote); up to 30 % chemical cut cited from ministry studies, unverified
Effort
high
Risks
Vendor-only evidence; drift and chemical-safety rules; drone licensing; displaced field labour.

How to adopt

Trial spraying drones on a small share of fields with a distributor; train operators; check licensing and spray rules.

How a room runs it

the ROOM for a paddy estate: the estate manager, the field-operations lead, the drone operator and an agronomy teammate (an agent definition with the rice-farming skills); the agent reads the estate's plot list and the drone operator's flight log and GENERATES the week's spray and spread jobs for the operator as plan steps with owners and due dates (plot, product, window), and raises a decision in the manager's Inbox when a plot's chemical use passes its envelope (approve more / hold, with a deadline); the humans keep the flying, the sign-off and the spend above the envelope; the receipt records each finished job with plot, product and date; budgets degrade before they block

The engagement on top

a custom engagement: the estate's own systems wired to the room through connectors loaded on this pull (the plot register or ERP, the drone operator's flight log, the stock sheet), an agronomist as the paid professional on the match, and the sector pack's task templates for spraying and spreading rounds; operators reached over WhatsApp

Source: vendor · 2025 · vendor only; to corroborate

Community-service pilot: assembled agro-drones sprayed pesticide on three farmers' rice fields in Majannang village, Gowa, South Sulawesi (about 1 L of mixture over about 180 m2 in about 9 minutes); terraced fields made spraying less effective

Where
ID, Southeast Asia
Segment
SMB (smallholder farmers)
Problem
smallholders cannot afford drones or the skill to run them; terraced plots
Technology
agricultural drone (assembled by the team), pesticide spraying
Who uses it
three farmers in Majannang village, Parigi district, Gowa regency (Indonesia); an eight-author university-style team (affiliation not stated on the page)
Outcome
About 1 L of mixture over about 180 m2 in about 9 minutes on three farms; terraced fields made the result not optimal (the authors, SNP2M 2024)
Effort
medium
Risks
Terraced fields cut effectiveness; very small sample; pesticide handling safety.

How to adopt

Pilot a drone-spraying service on a few plots; compare time and coverage with manual spraying; account for terrain.

How a room runs it

the ROOM for a smallholder group: the farmer group's chair, the three to thirty farmers, the drone service provider and an agronomy teammate; the agent reads the farmers' plot list (plot, crop, date of last spray) and GENERATES the spraying round as plan steps for the provider (which plots, which day, which product) and a decision for each farmer (accept the service and its fee, with a deadline) in their Inbox over WhatsApp; the humans keep the flying, the consent and the payment; the receipt records the plot, the product and the date for each farmer; the shared bill splits the provider's fee across the farmers served

The engagement on top

a custom engagement: the farmer group's plot register (a sheet or the cooperative's member list) wired to the room through a connector loaded on this pull, a drone service provider or extension officer as the paid professional on the match, and the sector pack's task templates for group service rounds

Source: paper · 2025

Photo-based crop diagnosis in a farmer app: the farmer photographs a pest or disease problem, an image model returns a diagnosis and crop-protection advice, geotagged uploads trigger area early warnings; features work offline; Indonesia in progressive rollout

Where
ID;IN;PK;TH;BD, Southeast Asia;South Asia
Segment
SMB (smallholder farmers)
Problem
pests and diseases misdiagnosed; advice reaches smallholders late
Technology
Cropwise Grower app, Plantix image recognition (50+ crops, 500+ diseases), offline mode
Who uses it
Syngenta Asia Pacific with Plantix; rollout in India, Pakistan, Indonesia, Thailand and Bangladesh
Outcome
93 % accuracy and 500,000 farmers targeted (Syngenta's own figures)
Effort
low
Risks
Misdiagnosis harms crops; vendor figures unverified; input-sales conflict of interest.

How to adopt

Offer farmers a photo-diagnosis app that works offline; train extension agents; link advice to locally available inputs.

How a room runs it

the ROOM for a farmer group with an extension officer: the farmers, the group's chair and an agronomy teammate; a farmer posts a photo of the problem in the room over WhatsApp and the agent reads the diagnosis the farmer's app already gives, then GENERATES a task for the farmer (inspect the neighbouring plot by Thursday, spray only if confirmed) and a decision for the extension officer or the group's agronomist (confirm the treatment, with a deadline); the humans keep the diagnosis sign-off and the spend on chemicals; the receipt records the photo, the verdict and the treatment done; the agent never diagnoses on its own model

The engagement on top

a custom engagement: the farmer group's member and plot list wired to the room through a connector, the input retailer's price list, an agronomist or extension officer as the paid professional on the match, and the sector pack's task templates for pest and disease rounds; Bahasa messages over WhatsApp

Source: vendor · 2022 · vendor only; to corroborate

Digital Village for oil palm smallholders: an app with fertiliser dosage per farm and harvest and maintenance records, an always-on Q&A service, an online input shop, and prices the cooperative unit no longer has to relay by hand

Where
ID, Southeast Asia
Segment

Karya Harapan Mukti village, Bungo regency, Jambi; the village cooperative unit (KUD Karya Mukti); SawitPRO (Indonesia)

none stated
Effort
medium

Outcomes unmeasured; connectivity; data ownership by the cooperative versus the vendor.

the ROOM for a village cooperative: the cooperative's chair, the smallholders, the village head and a palm agronomy teammate; the agent reads the harvest and maintenance records the farmers already keep and GENERATES each farmer's fertiliser and upkeep tasks with due dates, and the cooperative's weekly collection plan as steps for the chair; a decision lands in the chair's Inbox when an input order passes the cooperative's envelope (approve / split the order, with a deadline); the humans keep the weighing, the price and the payment; the receipt records each lot and each input order, and the shared bill splits a group purchase among the members

The engagement on top

a custom engagement: the cooperative's member register and weighbridge sheet wired to the room through connectors loaded on this pull, a cooperative accountant or agronomist as the paid professional on the match, and the sector pack's task templates for smallholder upkeep rounds; farmers reached over WhatsApp

Traceability app for independent oil palm smallholders: farmers' plots are mapped and fresh-fruit-bunch origin is traced so mills can accept the bunches; data collected from 3,132 farmers in five locations over about three years

ID, Southeast Asia
Segment
public / NGO with smallholders and mills
Problem
independent smallholders risk exclusion from supply chains that demand traceability; mills must prove origin
Technology
Hamurni mapping and traceability app
Who uses it
WWF-Indonesia; independent oil palm smallholders in Pelalawan and Kuantan Singingi (Riau), Katingan (Central Kalimantan), Kapuas Hulu and Sintang (West Kalimantan); palm oil mills

the ROOM for a smallholder group selling to a mill: the group's chair, the farmers, the mill's buyer and a traceability teammate; the agent reads the plot records the farmers already hold and GENERATES the pre-harvest steps (confirm plot boundary, record harvest date, attach the delivery) for each farmer with due dates, and a decision for the buyer (accept the lot, with a deadline); the humans keep the harvest, the weighing and the acceptance; the receipt is the lot's record from plot to delivery, a file a buyer can verify

The engagement on top

a custom engagement: the group's plot register or the mill's intake system wired to the room through connectors loaded on this pull, a certification or sustainability professional as the paid professional on the match, and the sector pack's task templates for lot preparation and compliance files

Sensor-driven automatic fish and shrimp feeders: the feeder gauges appetite, dispenses feed and sends consumption reports to the farmer's phone; company claimed an average 21 % cut in feed use

Where
ID, Southeast Asia
Segment
SMB and mid (aquaculture)
Problem

eFishery (Indonesia); fish and shrimp farmers

high

The engagement on top

a custom engagement: connectors loaded on this pull to the team's record system and diary; a clinical lead as the paid professional on the match who decides what may be recorded; the mental-health pack's care-plan-review and letter templates

the platform supports portfolios of more than AED 22 billion (about USD 6 billion) in real estate assets (the company's own scale figure, not a measured change; not attributed on the page)
Effort
medium
Risks
Vendor claims only; fair-housing and affordability checks bias; unsupervised agent actions.

How to adopt

Needs property, lease and payment data in one place. Start with rent collection and renewal reminders with manager approval. Running it needs integration to payment systems.

How a room runs it

the ROOM for a rental portfolio: the property manager, the landlord, the leasing and collections staff and a renewals teammate; the teammate reads the leases, rent ledger and arrears the manager already keeps and GENERATES the tasks as plan steps (send renewal offers for the 14 leases ending in 60 days, chase the three overdue units, book the inspection), and a rent change or a legal notice lands in the landlord's or manager's Inbox as a decision with a deadline; the humans keep the approvals, the tenant conversation and the notice; the receipt records each renewal signed and each payment received

The engagement on top

the manager's rental ledger, lease store and bank feed wired to the room through connectors loaded on this pull; a property lawyer or licensed manager as the paid professional on the match; the rental pack's renewal and arrears templates; tenants are reached on WhatsApp

Religious organisations S94

Researched in Community & civic

Adopt first

Needs a bank partner for QR codes and a donation account per mosque. Start with QR codes on donation boxes in a few mosques. Running it needs treasurers trained and monthly reporting.

BSI and the Indonesian Mosque Council (DMI) pilot mosque digitalisation in 37 Aceh mosques: QRIS codes on donation boxes send infak and zakat straight to the mosque's account, a mosque finance and activity app, and crowdfunding for waqf projects; about 300,000 of nearly 800,000 mosques are registered in the Religious Ministry's SIMAS

Where
ID, Southeast Asia
Segment
community (mosques)
Problem
cash donations, manual mosque books, weak transparency
Technology
QRIS, mobile banking, mosque management app, crowdfunding
Who uses it
Bank Syariah Indonesia, DMI, mosque committees; Ministry of Religious Affairs (SIMAS)
Outcome
DMI secretary-general says mosques using QRIS can raise income up to 10 times (an official's estimate, no data)
Effort
medium
Risks
Fraud with fake QR codes; digital divide; claim of 10x is unmeasured. No AI.

How to adopt

Needs a bank partner for QR codes and a donation account per mosque. Start with QR codes on donation boxes in a few mosques. Running it needs treasurers trained and monthly reporting.

How a room runs it

the ROOM for a mosque: the chair of the takmir, the treasurer, the imam and a mosque-admin teammate; the agent reads the donation records the mosque already has and GENERATES the monthly report for the congregation as a draft for the treasurer, the Friday roster tasks for volunteers with due dates and a proposal for the chair when a spend exceeds the committee's envelope; the committee keeps every fund decision and the imam all religious guidance, the agent gives none; the receipt is the open book the congregation can read

The engagement on top

connectors loaded on this pull to the mosque's bank statement export and SIMAS records; a community accountant as paid professional; the pack carries roster and report templates; channel: WhatsApp group of the congregation

Source: press · 2021
